_what: The idea library for the weekly client emails (Guy, 25 Oct 2026). Every weekly email carries ONE idea from here, in Guy's words with a credit. Sources: books (all 19 kept by Guy), Guy's own Mindset Mastery editions, and a shortlist of Beth Berghan's emails (Guy rates each Best / Good / Skip on the rating page; Skip never goes). Links are asset-library keys ({{asset:key}}) - at most one optional Watch link per email, not every week. Never repeat an idea to a client who has had it (their Touch Note and touch record say what went).

books.title: Give and Take
books.author: Adam Grant
books.idea: Givers end up at the top - when they give to the right people and protect themselves from takers.
books.angle: The heart of the good guys network.

link.talk: Are you a giver or a taker?

books.title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
books.author: Stephen R. Covey
books.idea: Begin with the end in mind; put first things first.
books.angle: Plan backwards from the goal; make time for the important.
books.note: FranklinCovey video; Covey himself may not be on screen

books.title: Atomic Habits
books.author: James Clear
books.idea: Small daily systems beat big goals; every action is a vote for who you are becoming.
books.angle: Make networking a daily habit, not a burst.

books.title: Essentialism
books.author: Greg McKeown
books.idea: If you do not prioritise your life, someone else will.

link.talk: Essentialism - The Disciplined Pursuit of Less

books.title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
books.author: Dale Carnegie
books.idea: Be genuinely interested in others; let them talk about themselves.

link.talk: Become Genuinely Interested in Other People

books.title: Never Eat Alone
books.author: Keith Ferrazzi
books.idea: Build relationships before you need them; generosity is the currency.
books.angle: Almost a manual for the method.

link.talk: 40 Years Of Networking Advice In 7 Minutes

books.title: The Go-Giver
books.author: Bob Burg and John David Mann
books.idea: Your worth is how much more you give in value than you take in payment.
books.angle: Warm, story-based; suits the inner circle.

link.talk: A Quick and Really Fun Overview of The Go-Giver

books.title: Who Not How
books.author: Dan Sullivan and Benjamin Hardy
books.idea: Ask "who can help?" instead of "how do I do this?".

link.talk: Who Not How: The Formula for Achieving Bigger Goals

books.title: The Slight Edge
books.author: Jeff Olson
books.idea: Small, easy actions done daily compound - and are easy not to do.
books.note: Channel named Jeff Olson - not proven to be his own

books.title: The Compound Effect
books.author: Darren Hardy
books.idea: Small smart choices, plus consistency, plus time, make the big result.

link.talk: Darren Hardy Intro of The Compound Effect

books.title: Eat That Frog
books.author: Brian Tracy
books.idea: Do your most important task first, before the day takes over.
books.angle: Time management for the busy ones.

link.talk: Eat That Frog & The ABCDE Method

books.title: Influence
books.author: Robert Cialdini
books.idea: Reciprocity, liking and social proof drive people to say yes.
books.angle: Why giving first and introductions work.

books.title: Think and Grow Rich
books.author: Napoleon Hill
books.idea: The mastermind: minds working together beat one alone.
books.angle: The inner circle as a mastermind.
books.note: No official short talk - idea only

books.title: Start with Why
books.author: Simon Sinek
books.idea: People do not buy what you do, they buy why you do it.
books.angle: Positioning, for clients who struggle with it.

books.title: Mindset
books.author: Carol Dweck
books.idea: Abilities grow with effort; setbacks are learning, not verdicts.
books.angle: Clients new to the tech who feel behind.

link.talk: The power of believing that you can improve

books.title: Grit
books.author: Angela Duckworth
books.angle: The patience curve - results take weeks.

link.talk: Grit: The power of passion and perseverance

books.title: The Speed of Trust
books.author: Stephen M.R. Covey
books.idea: Trust is a skill that makes everything faster and cheaper.

books.title: Deep Work
books.author: Cal Newport
books.idea: Focused, uninterrupted time produces the work that matters.

books.title: Super Connector
books.author: Scott Gerber and Ryan Paugh
books.idea: Connectors create value by linking the right people, not by collecting contacts.
books.angle: Roland and Sam are natural examples.
books.note: No official short talk - idea only

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Interested beats interesting
mindsetMastery.idea: Being curious about other people builds connection faster than trying to impress them.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: You're measuring yourself against a world that's gone
mindsetMastery.idea: Experienced people shrink around AI by judging themselves on old rules. Their judgement still matters.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: How many tabs do you have open?
mindsetMastery.idea: Too many open loops make a busy day feel empty. Close a few to feel real progress.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Consistency Isn't Sexy
mindsetMastery.idea: Boring basics, repeated without negotiating with yourself, give results you can rely on.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Do you need Motivation or Momentum?
mindsetMastery.idea: Motivation is a mood that comes and goes. Momentum from small started actions keeps you moving.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Easy To Work With, Or Easy To Overlook?
mindsetMastery.idea: Being reliable and low-fuss can make you invisible unless you also speak up about your value.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery - Memory Dividends Don't Wait
mindsetMastery.idea: Experiences compound like money, so make meaningful memories now rather than later.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Why "Follow Your Passion" Might Be Bad Advice
mindsetMastery.idea: Passion usually grows from skill and mastery rather than coming first.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Cut the Noise, Keep the Focus
mindsetMastery.idea: Pick the one goal that matters and let the rest of the noise go.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: The Power of Really Listening
mindsetMastery.idea: Really listening is a bold move. People trust and remember the person who truly heard them.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Do the Opposite
mindsetMastery.idea: Flip an autopilot routine on purpose to get fresh thinking and different results.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Stop Spinning - Start Solving
mindsetMastery.idea: Swap going round in circles about a problem for one small concrete next step.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Let Others Sing Your Praises
mindsetMastery.idea: You can't sell yourself well, but people in genuine relationships with you will do it for you.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Stop Replaying Conversations That Are Already Over
mindsetMastery.idea: Take the lesson from a finished conversation, then stop replaying it in your head.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Ownership Isn't Automatic
mindsetMastery.idea: You can't force people to take ownership. You invite it with trust, clarity and space.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Micro-Habits for All-Day Energy
mindsetMastery.idea: Small habits through the day keep your energy steady instead of crashing.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: I wish someone had told me
mindsetMastery.idea: Lessons most of us learn the hard way, passed on so others can skip the pain.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Say It Sooner
mindsetMastery.idea: Have the tricky conversation early, before it grows into a tough one.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Let Them
mindsetMastery.idea: Stop trying to control what other people do. Put your energy into how you respond.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Deep Work
mindsetMastery.idea: Guard blocks of distraction-free time for the work that really moves things.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Win the Morning, Win the Day
mindsetMastery.idea: A deliberate morning routine sets the tone for everything that follows.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Control the Controllables
mindsetMastery.idea: Spend your energy on what you can influence, not on what you can't.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Don't Wait for a Restructure to Reinvent Yourself
mindsetMastery.idea: Reinvent yourself and stay visible before change forces your hand.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: The Power of One More
mindsetMastery.idea: Doing one more rep, call or attempt past where you'd stop adds up to real growth.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: The Psychology of Influence
mindsetMastery.idea: Persuasion follows learnable principles like reciprocity, liking and social proof.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Age Is a State of Mind
mindsetMastery.idea: Getting older can't be avoided, but growing old in your outlook is optional.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Break the Brules
mindsetMastery.idea: Question the rules you inherited and never chose. Many no longer serve you.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Respect Is Hard Won (and Easily Lost)
mindsetMastery.idea: Respect takes years to build and one careless moment to lose.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: The Speed of Trust
mindsetMastery.idea: When trust is high, everything moves faster and costs less.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Do Less, But Better
mindsetMastery.idea: Choose the few things that matter most and do them well, or others will choose for you.

mindsetMastery.subject: Mindset Mastery: Givers, Takers, and Matchers
mindsetMastery.idea: Generous givers who protect themselves from takers end up most successful.

beth.subject: Ever Considered That The Room Is Reading You Too?
beth.idea: People pick up your mood and energy before you say a word, and it sets the tone.
beth.angle: In a first coffee, the other person is quietly deciding whether you're safe to introduce. Your presence answers that.

beth.subject: Ever Wondered Why They're Not Picking You?
beth.idea: Being overlooked is often about how your message lands, not about what you can do.
beth.angle: People only refer you if they can explain what you do in one clear sentence.

beth.subject: Want to Build Trust Quickly? Start with These Two Phrases
beth.idea: Two small phrases build trust fast: asking what the other person thinks, and admitting you could be wrong.
beth.angle: Asking for a contact's view makes the conversation shared, which makes them want to help you.

beth.subject: Small Talk, Big Impact: 5 Ways to Connect Confidently
beth.idea: Small talk done well isn't small. It's how connection starts, and you don't need to be loud.
beth.angle: Every referral relationship starts with a few easy minutes of chat. Get good at them.

beth.subject: Timeless Strategies for Networking Like a Pro
beth.idea: Confident connections with peers, clients and leaders come from simple, repeatable networking habits.
beth.angle: Networking is a learnable routine, not a personality type.

beth.subject: What If He Hadn't Asked?
beth.idea: Two tied Olympic high jumpers shared gold because one simply asked if they could.
beth.angle: The introduction you want often isn't offered until you have the courage to ask for it.

beth.subject: Your Reputation's Talking. Are You Listening?
beth.idea: Your reputation is what people say when you're not there, and it's set by how you act on hard days.
beth.angle: A referral is your reputation spoken out loud by someone else. Act like it.

beth.subject: Why Admitting You Don't Have the Answer Can Be a Power Move
beth.idea: Saying you don't know is a strength, not a weakness. It builds credibility.
beth.angle: 'I don't know, but I know a guy' is the most trusted sentence in a referral network.

beth.subject: Are You Missing The Connection That Comes From Deep, Valuable Conversations?
beth.idea: Move past weather-and-health chat to conversations that really matter to both people.
beth.angle: Deeper conversations turn contacts into people who know you well enough to vouch for you.

beth.subject: Feel Disconnected At Home and At Work? These Habits Might Be Why
beth.idea: Connection rarely ends with a fight. It fades quietly through small habits of neglect.
beth.angle: Networks die from silence, not conflict. Regular light touches keep them alive.

beth.subject: Scheduling Is The Answer To Finding Harmony In Work And Play
beth.idea: 'Let's definitely catch up' means nothing until it's in the calendar. Your calendar shows your real priorities.
beth.angle: Turn every 'we should catch up' into a booked time on the spot.

beth.subject: If performance was enough, you'd already be further ahead
beth.idea: Good work alone isn't enough. Image and exposure decide who gets opportunities too.
beth.angle: Your network is your exposure. Capable people stay stuck when too few people know their work.

beth.subject: Some People Excel At Real Friendship And Some Don't - Which One Are You?
beth.idea: Online likes are not friendship. Real relationships need effort, presence and showing up.
beth.angle: A thousand connections are worth less than a dozen people who would pick up the phone for you.

beth.subject: Your Time
beth.idea: Rushing past people and giving them scraps of attention costs more than it saves.
beth.angle: Full, unhurried attention is the cheapest way to be remembered warmly.

beth.subject: It's Not The Phone. It's Actually You
beth.idea: When someone checks their phone mid-chat, it's often a sign the conversation lost them, not the phone's fault.
beth.angle: Keep conversations about the other person and they'll stay with you.

beth.subject: Asking Better Questions Is The Answer
beth.idea: A well-chosen question sparks more insight and connection than any clever statement.
beth.angle: Good questions in a first meeting tell you who they could help, and who could help them.

beth.subject: The Hidden Impact: Rethinking Habits for a More Visible Success
beth.idea: Capable people feel undervalued because quiet habits keep their contribution invisible.
beth.angle: If nobody can see your work, nobody can recommend it. Small visibility habits fix that.

beth.subject: You Don't Need More Confidence. You Need Evidence.
beth.idea: Confidence comes from looking at what you've already achieved, not from waiting to feel ready.
beth.angle: Keep a list of your wins and you'll ask for introductions without flinching.

beth.subject: Stop Treating Discomfort Like a Red Flag.
beth.idea: The awkward, clunky feeling of something new is usually growth, not a warning to stop.
beth.angle: The first few networking conversations feel awkward. That's normal, so push through it.

beth.subject: Correcting with Compassion: How to Maintain Relationships When You Disagree
beth.idea: You can disagree with or correct someone without damaging the relationship.
beth.angle: Long-term referral partners will disagree sometimes. Handle it so the bond survives.

beth.subject: The Bold Move That Fuels Your Growth and Builds Leadership Intelligence
beth.idea: Asking for feedback feels awkward but is one of the fastest ways to grow.
beth.angle: Ask happy clients how they'd describe you. That's the exact wording your referrers should use.

beth.subject: You're Allowed To Want What You Want
beth.idea: If you stay quiet about what you want, other people fill in the blanks for you.
beth.angle: Be specific about the introductions you want, or you'll get random ones or none.

beth.subject: Stop Apologising for Taking Up Space
beth.idea: Needless apologies teach people to take you less seriously. Save sorry for real mistakes.
beth.angle: Drop 'sorry to bother you' from outreach. Reaching out is not an imposition.

beth.subject: If it mattered, you'd have done it by now
beth.idea: 'Too busy' is often a cover for avoiding the thing that matters.
beth.angle: The follow-up you keep postponing is usually the one that counts most.

beth.subject: Want To Be The Kind Of Leader That People Still Talk About?
beth.idea: People remember for decades how a leader made them feel, good or bad.
beth.angle: The people who still talk about you years later are your best source of referrals.

beth.subject: The Mirror Test: Are You Modelling What You're Asking For?
beth.idea: Before asking others to change, check whether you're showing the behaviour you want.
beth.angle: If you want referrals, be the person who gives them first.

beth.subject: Why Making New Friends As An Adult Can Be Hard (And What To Do About It)
beth.idea: Adult friendships don't happen by accident. They need deliberate effort and repeated contact.
beth.angle: Business relationships work the same way. Plan to see people again, or you won't.

beth.subject: You. Need. Connection.
beth.idea: Being curious about strangers' stories, like a rideshare driver's, builds real human connection.
beth.angle: Curiosity about everyone's story is how unexpected connections and referrals start.

beth.subject: You may be asking the wrong question
beth.idea: A lost season isn't failure but a step on the way. Reframe the question you're asking.
beth.angle: A coffee that led nowhere isn't failure. It's a seed that may come back later.

beth.subject: Time To Realise: You're Allowed to Outgrow Your Own Narrative.
beth.idea: 'I'm just not good at that' is often an old story, not a fact.
beth.angle: 'I'm not a networker' is a story you can retire.

beth.subject: How You Start Matters
beth.idea: The energy and intention you bring at the start of the week shapes the whole week.
beth.angle: Start the week with one relationship-building action and the week follows.

beth.subject: Nice Isn't Always Kind - And That's a Problem!
beth.idea: Being nice avoids hard truths. Being kind tells people what they need to hear, with care.
beth.angle: Trusted advisers are kind rather than nice, and that's why people refer them.

beth.subject: Stop Teaching People You're Always Free
beth.idea: Replying instantly every time trains people to expect it, and that becomes exhausting.
beth.angle: Protect time for relationship building instead of letting instant replies eat it.

beth.subject: Do You Realise That When You Say Nothing, You Are Still Saying Something
beth.idea: Staying silent sends a message too, often agreement or not caring.
beth.angle: Silence after a meeting or an introduction says something. Fill it with a follow-up.

beth.subject: If You're Already Tired It's Time To Edit Not Add
beth.idea: When you're worn out, cut things before you add anything new.
beth.angle: Drop low-value busywork to make room for the few relationships that matter.

beth.subject: Every Time You Let It Slide, You Set a Standard.
beth.idea: Each 'just this once' quietly becomes the standard you actually live by.
beth.angle: Skip your weekly outreach once and skipping becomes the habit.

beth.subject: When Great Ideas Fall Flat (and What to Do About It)
beth.idea: Good ideas get ignored when they're poorly delivered, then cheered when someone else says them.
beth.angle: How you pitch your value decides whether people repeat it to others.

beth.subject: Why Talking To Strangers May Be A Key Ingredient To A Joyful Day
beth.idea: Brief chats with strangers lift your mood and rebuild everyday human connection.
beth.angle: Practising easy chats with strangers makes networking feel natural.

beth.subject: The First No Is Always The Hardest
beth.idea: The first clean 'no' without over-justifying is the hardest. After that it gets easier.
beth.angle: Saying no to the wrong things frees time for the right relationships.

beth.subject: Beyond the Complaint Cycle: Navigating Unconscious Behaviours for Positive Impressions
beth.idea: Habitual complaining drains people and quietly shapes how others see you.
beth.angle: Nobody refers a complainer. Positive energy makes you easy to recommend.
